title: Adaptive stream developer provisioning and tool contracts - PRD notes
body:
Purpose
---
This is an engineering-focused PRD-sketch for an Adaptive Stream developer provisioning flow and a cleaner tool-contract surface on the Hosted API. Goal: reduce friction for teams using streaming+tool-calls while giving us deterministic fallback behavior when toollets fail or return malformed structured output.

Context and motivation
---
We get recurring asks from early adopters: "How do we wire our 3rd-party microtools into Hosted streaming without huge SDK lift?" Also, teams signal breakage when tool handlers respond slowly or return schema drift during partial responses. Existing SDKs assume a single canonical tool invocation path; that leads to brittle client integrations (retries explode, long tail latencies).

High level proposal
---
1) Developer provisioning manifest: a small JSON contract uploaded by a developer that declares the set of tool capabilities, preferred latency envelope, and output shape examples. The manifest is optional but when present allows the runtime to gate-favor fast-paths (prefetch warm slots, select shallow-cached model variants).

2) Tool contracts at the stream frame level: extend streaming frames to include a compact contract header for each tool call. Header fields (strings): tool_id, expected_schema_version, max_wait_ms, and graceful_fallback_hint (one of: noop | stale-cache | alternate-tool-id).

3) Sketch of SDK ergonomics: SDKs expose two surfaces: (a) declarative provision(manifest) and (b) non-blocking tool adapters with simple callback shapes. Developers can opt into optimistic-tool-mode where the client receives partial content while a background tool-call resolves; or blocking-tool-mode where the tool call is awaited within a turn.

User stories
---
- As a product engineer, I want the Hosted API to know my available toollets and their SLA so it can route lower-latency paths for interactive flows.
- As an SDK user, I want an ergonomic fallback that returns a minimal synthetic response when my tool times out, so the UI can remain responsive.
- As platform ops, I want telemetry hooks that show per-tool tail latency percentiles and schema failure rates.

Goals and success metrics
---
Primary goals:
- Developer onboarding time to first streaming tool demo <= 30 minutes with manifest.
- Reduce user-visible tool-timeout incidents by 60% for users who upload a manifest.
- Provide SDK primitives so 90% of instrumented clients follow fallback contracts without bespoke glue.

Metrics (examples to track):
- time_to_first_tool_call_success (median, p95)
- percent_of_streams_with_graceful_fallback_used
- tool_schema_validation_failure_rate
- client_library adoption: percentage of new integrations using provision(manifest)

Non-goals
---
- We are not building a fully-managed tool execution sandbox (no execution runtime for customer tool code). This is about advertising capabilities and graceful fallbacks, not hosting arbitrary user code.
- Not addressing enterprise private-deploy flow yet (this is hosted-first).

Detailed design notes
---
Developer provisioning manifest (example):
- name: "search-tool-v1"
- tool_id: "com.example.search.v1"
- preferred_mode: "fast|accurate" (developer hint)
- sample_output: small array of 1-3 representative JSON objects (helps schema inference)
- latency_profile: {"p50": 50, "p95": 300} (optional numbers in ms)
- fallback_policy: "noop|cached|proxy"

When a manifest is uploaded (via Console or API), the control plane stores a lightweight capability card used by the router and runtime to choose options: prewarm slots, favor cached responses, or route to an alternate replica.

Tool contract in stream frames
- Add an optional header in tool-invocation frames:
  - tool_id: string
  - expected_schema_tag: string (opaque tag representing developer declared schema)
  - max_wait_ms: integer
  - fallback_hint: string (noop|stale-cache|alternate-tool)
  - correlation_id: string (for client/trace correlation)

Runtime semantics:
- If tool call completes within max_wait_ms: attach tool result frame to stream and validate against expected_schema_tag. If validation fails, mark telemetry and emit a structured-error frame with an error-code and a JSON sample of problem.
- If tool call exceeds max_wait_ms: emit a graceful-fallback frame with fallback_hint applied. If fallback_hint==alternate-tool, the runtime will attempt a configured alternate-tool-id once.

SDK ergonomics (developer facing):
- provision(manifestJson) -> returns a capability_token (short TTL) and local hints (e.g., recommend_fastpath=true).
- createStream(opts) where opts can include fallback_mode: optimistic | conservative.
- toolAdapter.register(tool_id, {invoke: async (payload)=>{}}) - the SDK automatically serializes out-of-band tool call results back to the server if run in client-assisted mode.
- local validation helpers: sdk.validateSchema(tag, obj) and sdk.suggestSchema(sampleArray) to help generate sample_output during provisioning.

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs)
---
- How to version expected_schema_tag? Use hash of canonical JSON schema, or opaque developer-provided string? (Tradeoffs: discoverability vs strict validation.)
- Security: manifests may leak info about backend capabilities. Need RBAC for who can read manifests in an org.
- Billing: Do we charge for prewarm slots triggered by manifests? Propose to surface prewarm as optional add-on for Dedicated customers.
- Can alternate-tool be another hosted model (redwood-model-x) or only developer-provided toollets?

Telemetry + observability plan
---
Event types to emit: manifest_uploaded, tool_invocation_started, tool_invocation_finished(success|error|timeout|schema_fail), fallback_applied, schema_validation_sample.
Minimum dashboards: per-tool latency histogram, schema-failure rate, percentage of streams using optimistic fallback. Provide drilldown by customer, API key, and SDK version.

Migration plan and rollout phases
---
Phase 0 (internals, canary): implement frame header, basic timeout handling, and telemetry for internal teams. Expose a hidden Console flag to upload manifests. (2 sprints)
Phase 1 (public beta): SDK primitives (JS/Go) with provision(manifest) + example repo. Beta customers invited. (4–6 sprints)
Phase 2 (GA): Console UX polish, managed prewarm add-on, billing telemetry, and default safe fallback behavior.

Operational considerations
---
- Runtime must ensure fallback decisions are idempotent for replayed/resumed streams. Use correlation_id to dedupe.
- Validate manifests asynchronously: accept upload, run lightweight schema inference, then mark manifest live. If inference fails, surface warnings in Console.

Implementation risks
---
- Schema drift: developers may upload incomplete or unrepresentative samples leading to false positives in validation. Mitigation: provide SDK sampling tools and warn when variance high.
- Client fragmentation: if SDKs behave differently across languages on fallback semantics we will create support burden. Mitigation: canonical behavior tests and interop suite.

Open deliverables (owners)
---
- API: POST /provisioning/manifests (Ava)
- Runtime: frame header parsing + fallback engine (Miguel)
- SDKs: JS + Go provision() and toolAdapter (Priya)
- Console: manifest upload + reporting UI (Jordan)
- Telemetry: taxonomy and dashboards (SRE analytics)

Quick UX notes for Console
---
- Minimal upload flow: paste a sample_output JSON + provide tool_id + optional latency hints.
- Console shows a quick summary: inferred schema fields, flagged mismatches, recommended fallback policy.
- Ability to mark a manifest as "preview" or "live".

Questions for next sync
---
- Should manifests be encrypted at rest tied to API keys? (Security asks).
- Do we allow multi-tenant tools declared in a shared manifest? (Yes/no).
- What default max_wait_ms should the Console recommend for interactive chat vs background jobs?

Notes to engineers:
- Start small: structural header + timeout-before-fallback is the core value. The manifest-driven prewarm is an optimizer, not required for MVP.
- Keep frames compact — we want the header to be optional so older SDKs still interop.

Appendix: example stream flow (simplified)
- Client starts stream, passes capability_token (optional).
- LLM emits text chunk and indicates tool-call frame: {tool_id:search.v1, max_wait_ms:200} in header.
- Runtime forks tool-call, but emits partial content from model while waiting.
- If tool returns within 180ms -> attach structured tool frame and re-score step.
- If tool times out at 200ms -> runtime emits fallback frame (fallback_hint=stale-cache) and continues.

TODO: flesh out wire-format examples and add unit tests for schema_failure path.

End of notes (working doc).
